facts.raw_span: A 64-year-old woman with a 20-year history of hypertension
presented with dizziness and head discomfort of 3 days’ duration
Her blood pressure at presentation was 190/100 mmHg
no abdominal pain, melena, hematemesis, or dysphagia
a 4.7 cm × 4.4 cm hypoechoic lesion with a clear, regular boundary located between the upper pole of the spleen and the abdominal aorta
the lesion appeared to originate from the stomach and suggested a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST)
Vital signs were within normal limits
Physical examination was unremarkable
routine blood tests, blood biochemistry, fecal occult blood, and tumor markers were all normal
a 5.5 cm × 4.3 cm smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass in the gastric wall protruding beyond the serosal contour
surrounding lymph-node enlargement (nodes up to 1.0 cm)
a smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on the gastric fundus
